scope: Memory-object registry records use the existing memory_capability_nodes byte/count admission, alongside capability/namespace/read-borrower metadata. Original backing-sponsor class follows private, published and detached nodes through physical completion and actual node deallocation. Numerical limits, the 22-pool inventory, statistics/register ABI and physical completion rules are unchanged.
artifact_note: Runtime Rust sources were frozen before all campaigns. Later documentation edits alter tracked-diff identities; source and archived artifact hashes identify the code exercised. Service source and ABI are unchanged; staged bundles were reused and runners regenerated signed security fixtures.

policy.capture: ChargedFrames captures platform_identity(owner.id()) == Some(exact_handle) before the generation-qualified page/object reservation and storage/frame allocation. Copy retains its existing source backing sponsorship separately from destination capability metadata. No later owner field, promotion or ASID lookup chooses a node refund.
policy.publication: ObjectStorage, object registry and RetiredObject use the same charged node type. Direct allocation/copy require three candidate nodes (capability, namespace, object); the third rejects before frame-vector/physical allocation and publication. Source pins and hidden authority cancel through the existing complete owners. Moves relink existing object ownership without reclassifying its charge.
policy.release: Physical success precedes payload/node disposal. The collection deallocates the actual node before metadata refund, then the original physical sponsorship charge releases. Prefix/physical failure or abandonment retains the complete private/published owner, original metadata charge and physical reservation, including consumed frame identities and exact old generation.
policy.decision: Keep defaults: actual empty 224-byte object-layout controls admit about 14000 ordinary candidates before byte exhaustion, with count headroom, above the 6144 ordinary object planning ceiling. This is a single-layout observation, not a promise that all mixed or independent ceilings can be occupied together. Shared storage competes within the same class; measured workloads may justify raising central limits. No holder allocation or new pool is introduced.
policy.constructor_boundary: The uncharged PreparedEntry convenience factory now compiles only under cfg(test). Current production sites use explicit charged construction; this does not establish all-kernel allocation admission.

remaining_limits: Object frame-vector capacity is not admitted by this patch.
Aggregate metadata principals, allocator bookkeeping and general heap admission remain open.
Serialized real-node pressure and kernel adapter controls do not establish sustained hostile concurrent EL0 fairness or wider caller/IRQ/latency qualification.
Node allocator and physical-release failures use injected adapters; native general heap OOM is not forced.
Existing deliberate backing-retention fixtures now retain their object-node admission too; no new physical page/root/authority-retention fixture was added.
Metadata quota or retained bytes grant no physical completion or retry authority.
